objective_for_doctor: A 65-year-old Female patient presents to the clinic. Chief complaint: I have noticed weakness in your facial muscles and/or eyes, previously, or do you currently, have any weakness/paralysis in one or more of your limbs or in your face, and foot numbness/tingling.

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?
Hello. For some time, I’ve noticed weakness in my facial muscles and/or my eyes. I also have tingling and numbness in my feet, and I’ve had weakness in my face and/or limbs before.

Doctor: I’m Dr. Agent—how quickly did the facial/eye weakness and the foot tingling start (sudden within hours/days vs gradual over weeks/months), and is it getting worse? Also, do you have double vision or trouble swallowing/breathing?  
Doctor: REQUEST TEST: Neurologic exam (cranial nerves, strength/reflexes, sensation), and basic labs (CBC, CMP, B12, TSH, HbA1c) plus MRI brain with/without contrast.

The facial/eye weakness started kind of not super fast—more like over days, not within just a few hours. The foot tingling also came on over days, and yes, I feel it has been getting worse.  

I don’t have double vision, and I don’t have trouble swallowing or breathing.

Doctor: Thanks—since this is subacute (days) and worsening with facial/eye weakness plus progressive foot tingling, I’m concerned about a neuropathy or central process; do you have numbness in your hands as well, and any new back pain or trouble walking/balance? Also, have you had recent infections (flu/COVID), new medications, or known diabetes/alcohol use?  
Doctor: REQUEST TEST: Electromyography/Nerve Conduction Studies (EMG/NCS) and Vitamin B12 level (if not already), plus Serum protein electrophoresis with immunofixation (SPEP/IFE)

I don’t have numbness in my hands. I also haven’t had new back pain, and I haven’t had trouble walking or balance that I can tell.  

I haven’t had any recent flu or COVID that I know of, no new medications, and I don’t have known diabetes or heavy alcohol use.

Doctor: I’d like to clarify: have you noticed any weight loss, frequent diarrhea, burning/tingling pain, or problems with bladder/bowel control—and do you have any rash, eye pain, or hearing changes?  
Doctor: Also, on exam I’m concerned about a pattern like Guillain-Barré/variant, CIDP, or a nutritional/immune neuropathy—please REQUEST TEST: Lumbar puncture with CSF analysis (cell count, protein, glucose, oligoclonal bands) and check ESR/CRP, and if available add CSF/serum autoimmune/paraneoplastic antibodies.

I haven’t noticed weight loss or frequent diarrhea. I do have tingling/burning-type numbness in my feet, but I don’t have bladder or bowel control problems. I also don’t have a rash, eye pain, or hearing changes.

I’m Dr. Agent—do you have any history of autoimmune disease (thyroid disease, lupus, Sjögren’s) or cancer, and have you had any recent dental/urinary infection or vaccination right before symptoms began? Also, when you say facial/eye weakness, is it more like difficulty closing one/both eyes or facial asymmetry, and do you have any leg weakness on top of the tingling?

I don’t know of any autoimmune disease or cancer history for me. I also don’t recall any recent dental or urinary infection, and I don’t remember a vaccination right before the symptoms started.  

For the facial/eye weakness, it feels more like difficulty with facial muscles and eye area weakness (I can’t fully close/keep eyes shut well at times), and yes—there’s some weakness in my legs along with the tingling.

Doctor: Thank you—difficulty closing/keeping eyes shut suggests facial/cranial nerve involvement (and with progressive leg weakness + sensory tingling over days), I’m most concerned about an immune-mediated neuropathy such as **Guillain-Barré spectrum** or **CIDP**, but we must also exclude central causes.  
Doctor: REQUEST TEST: Lumbar puncture results (I need CSF cell count + protein; add cytology if available) **and** REQUEST TEST: MRI spine (and brain report if already done), and I’ll also order respiratory monitoring (FVC/NIF) given the eyelid weakness.
Okay. I understand. I don’t have those test results yet, but I’m willing to do the lumbar puncture and the MRI, and I can do breathing measurements too.

Doctor: I’ll proceed assuming an immune neuropathy until proven otherwise—first, are you having any new shortness of breath when lying flat, trouble speaking clearly, or choking on liquids? Also, do you notice areflexia (feel like your reflexes are “sluggish”) or worsening weakness when you try to climb stairs.  
Doctor: REQUEST TEST: FVC and NIF (respiratory muscle strength) now, and a complete neurologic exam with reflexes documented (including knee/ankle and facial strength).

No, I’m not having new shortness of breath when lying flat, and I don’t have trouble speaking clearly or choking on liquids.  

I do feel weaker when I try to climb stairs, but I’m not sure about my reflexes—if they’re sluggish, I haven’t specifically checked that myself.

Doctor: Given the subacute, progressive facial/eyelid weakness with leg weakness and distal burning/tingling, immune neuropathy (Guillain–Barré spectrum vs CIDP) moves highest on the list; do you notice any decreased sensation to touch/vibration on your feet, and are your symptoms symmetric or more on one side?  
Doctor: DIAGNOSIS READY: Suspected immune-mediated polyradiculoneuropathy (Guillain–Barré spectrum vs CIDP) with cranial nerve involvement; needs CSF (albuminocytologic dissociation) and EMG/NCS plus MRI to exclude central causes and confirm subtype.
